description: Scope analysis for extending the benchmark to full routing

current_scope.protocol: Direct entanglement generation, fixed storage age
current_scope.routing: None — no Router, RuleSet, or EntanglementProtocol
current_scope.timing: Fixed attempt interval, fixed storage age
current_scope.what_is_tested: Whether both simulators apply the same channel correctly
current_scope.what_is_not_tested: Routing, swapping, queueing, contention, dead time

proposed_extensions.name: Three-node chain (A — B — C)
proposed_extensions.description: Add a repeater node B that swaps entanglement between A-C
new_components: SeQUeNCe Node at B with two memories (one for each link)
challenges: The two memories at B have different ages (one from A-B link, one from B-C link)
The swap occurs when both links succeed — the age is random
WestQuant requires exact age samples (no interpolation)
Need to export channels for the full range of possible ages

proposed_extensions.name: Star topology (hub with N spokes)
proposed_extensions.description: Central hub with N memories, each connected to a leaf node
new_components: Hub node with N memory slots
Scheduler that selects which links to attempt
challenges: Hub has limited memory — not all links can be served simultaneously
Need to model dead time (memory reset after readout)

proposed_extensions.name: Mesh with routing
proposed_extensions.description: Multiple nodes with multiple paths; routing protocol selects paths
new_components: Path selection based on link quality
challenges: Path selection depends on real-time link quality
Each hop adds a memory age — the total age is the sum of hop ages

key_questions.question: Does routing delay or channel decoherence dominate delivery probability?
key_questions.answer: Unknown — needs the three-node chain benchmark to measure
key_questions.method: Compare delivery probability at various distances with and without routing delay

key_questions.question: Can the WestQuant channel handle asynchronous retrieval?
key_questions.answer: Partially — the channel requires an exact age sample. A routing benchmark would need to generate ages from the routing timing distribution and export a channel for each possible age.
key_questions.method: Pre-compute channels on a fine age grid; look up the closest age at retrieval

key_questions.question: How does multi-hop entanglement affect fidelity?
key_questions.answer: Each swap adds noise. The WestQuant channel models a single write-store-read cycle. A multi-hop benchmark would need to compose channels across hops.
key_questions.method: Compose channels: F_total = F_hop1 * F_hop2 * ... * F_hopN

key_questions.question: What is the capacity limit of a repeater node?
key_questions.answer: Unknown — the current benchmark has no capacity contention. A star topology benchmark would measure how many simultaneous links a hub can serve.
key_questions.method: Vary the number of spokes and measure delivery probability per link

phase_1.name: Three-node chain
steps: Extend sequence_adapter.py with a RoutedProtocol class
Create a 3-node chain topology (A — B — C)
Generate ages from the link-generation timing distribution
Export channels for the full age range (0 to max_age)
Compare delivery probability against the direct-link benchmark
Identify whether routing or decoherence is the bottleneck

phase_2.name: Star topology with scheduling
steps: Add a hub node with N memory slots
Implement a scheduling policy (round-robin, priority, best-age)
Model dead time (memory reset after readout)
Measure delivery probability per link as a function of N

phase_3.name: Mesh with routing
steps: Add SeQUeNCe Router at each node
Measure end-to-end delivery probability across multiple paths
Compare routing strategies (shortest path vs best quality)

what_the_codebase_provides: memorylab/channels.py — Kraus operators and Choi matrices for channel export
